subsystems.name: Solar concentrator
subsystems.role: tracks the sun and focuses its light onto a receiver to charge the store during the lunar day.

subsystems.name: Thermal store
subsystems.role: holds gathered heat in processed regolith as sensible heat, hundreds of megajoules per cubic metre.
parts: sintered regolith bricks or packed granular bed

subsystems.name: Heat-transfer loop
subsystems.role: moves heat from receiver to store by day and from store to the engines by night.

subsystems.name: Power conversion
subsystems.role: turns stored heat into electricity on the cold, dark side of the cycle.

subsystems.name: Habitat thermal control
subsystems.role: shares the same hot mass to keep equipment and living volumes within temperature limits.

subsystems.name: Controls and robotics
subsystems.role: prepares the site, monitors charge state and manages daily cycling.
parts: excavator or rover for regolith handling

buildSteps.title: Pick and prepare the site
buildSteps.detail: A level area near the planned base is surveyed; regolith is bulldozed into berms and the ground compacted so the store and mirrors sit on stable footing.

buildSteps.title: Excavate and grade regolith
buildSteps.detail: Robotic excavators dig raw regolith, screen out large rocks and size the grains — fine dust is troublesome, so a controlled particle range is kept.

buildSteps.title: Form the storage body
buildSteps.detail: Sieved regolith is pressed into blocks or loaded into a containment shell, shaped so heat can be delivered and extracted efficiently.

buildSteps.title: Sinter the regolith
buildSteps.detail: Microwave or concentrated-solar heating fuses grain surfaces at roughly 1000–1100 °C, turning loose soil into a dense, thermally conductive solid that will not slump when hot.

buildSteps.title: Insulate and enclose
buildSteps.detail: The bed is wrapped in high-temperature insulation, with vacuum gaps and thin support struts, since in the lunar vacuum most loss is by radiation and conduction through contacts.

buildSteps.title: Install receiver and heat-transfer loop
buildSteps.detail: Concentrated sunlight heats a working fluid in the receiver; pipework and a blower circulate that fluid through channels in the regolith bed to charge it.

buildSteps.title: Add engines and radiators
buildSteps.detail: Stirling convertors draw heat from the store and reject waste heat to radiators sized for radiative cooling in vacuum, producing electricity through the night.

buildSteps.title: Commission and cycle
buildSteps.detail: The system is charged, held hot across the fourteen-day night, and discharged while temperature, flow and output are logged to prove stable cycling.

prerequisites.why: robotic digging and soil transport have been tested in analogue and simulant settings, but not at the scale of a working lunar plant.
microwave and solar sintering of simulants is demonstrated in laboratories; making large, crack-free, cycled blocks is the open question.
Stirling convertors have been built and tested for space power, so the conversion step is not the limiting factor.
materials must survive repeated swings from roughly 1000 °C to cryogenic night temperatures without cracking or sintering together.
controllers, radiators and autonomous operation through a 14-day night have not yet been combined into one fielded system.

pathway.milestone: simulant trials showing repeated charge and discharge cycles above 900 °C
pathway.unlocks: confidence that regolith is a workable storage medium and a baseline for sizing beds.

pathway.milestone: a small flight demonstrator that charges during the lunar day and powers a Stirling convertor through the night
pathway.unlocks: real data on heat loss, dust and thermal cycling on the Moon.

pathway.milestone: an integrated unit supplying night power and habitat heat for a robotic outpost
pathway.unlocks: nights-long operation without nuclear or battery-only backup, and a template for scaling.

pathway.milestone: regolith heat stores as one element of a lunar base energy architecture alongside solar arrays and fission surface power
pathway.unlocks: buffering for industrial processes such as oxygen extraction and metallurgy, where steady high-temperature heat matters more than electricity.
